newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends higher on short covering.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline ended higher Tuesday on a mixture of short covering in the outright price and fresh spread buying after gasoline tumbled seven cents a gallon over four sessions.
"I think most of the rise was short covering since gasoline had been so oversold," said Michael Busby, trader with Northville Industries in Melville, New York.

March gasoline settled up 0.43 cent a gallon at 63.96 cents while March crude settled four cents lower a barrel at $22.42. The March gasoline-to-crude crack spread rose to $4.40 a barrel from Monday $4.22.

A seasonal downturn in oil prices has bled some initial momentum from an upcoming rally in gasoline prices expected in early spring ahead of the summer driving season, dealer said. Consequently, some traders see a sharper rise in the gasoline crack rather than its outright price.
March heating oil ended 0.10 cent higher at 61.86 cents a gallon, with the back months weaker amid tight prompt supply.

A spate of refinery maintenance in the U.S. Gulf and a shift away from distillate output to make gasoline has tightened supply in U.S. Gulf. Cash traders cited distillate buying by major players such as Exxon and Chevron on Tuesday.

Also on Tuesday, Colonial Pipeline Co said it lifted its distillate line allocation program for February. In addition, Colonial said it will not likely resume any distillate line allocations this winter.
Colonial had rationed space on its huge pipeline that runs from Houston to the New York Harbor due to more shipping requests than its pipeline could handle.
Colonial Pipeline said now there is a lack of distillate demand in the New York Harbor due to seasonally mild temperatures recently for the key heating oil market of the northeastern United States.
But, demand for heat is expected to increase. The National Weather Service's six to 10 day forecast starting February 16 calls for below normal temperatures in the region.
With distillate tightness in the U.S. Gulf, New York Harbor supplies would therfore be replenished more slowly than before.

Meanwhile, dealers saw crude prices continuing their consolidation and establishing a new trading range of $21.50 to $23.50 for the next several weeks. Although crude's action made a higher low, Monday's low of $21.65 meant prompt crude had further room to fall, Northville's Busby said.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
